items.text: Readiness screen tells the truth when model service and sandbox are missing (names the exact fix, blocks Start, axe clean); a correct setup says Ready (in the browser journey). A stranger completing it unaided is I-07.
History search (Cmd+K), theme choice persisted across reload, framing line; axe clean in dark (journey checks)

Localisation scaffolding: all interface strings in typed catalogs, Hindi renders the main screens (journey checks in scripts/e2e), catalogs cannot drift (keys, placeholders, tags). Hindi text is machine-written and needs a native review; server-originated text stays English.
Parity registry classifies every catalog capability with a surface class and a trust reason; built ones carry evidence (classification only: it does not mean the capabilities are built)

Workflows beyond code review on the shared backend. Built: private memory with backup export and import, private chat, document questions with checked quotes (web, terminal, desktop), proposed fixes verified against the finding's reproducer and applied to the owner's files only when nothing changed (service, web screen and terminal /fixes and /applyfix). Not built: research with live sources (needs an egress and privacy decision), coding beyond reproducer-verified fixes, MCP exposure of fixes.
items.evidence_needed: journeys and hostile tests per workflow; registry rows move to BUILT_TESTED

items.text: Hosted mode at the confidential-host rung only (docs/engineering-decisions/hosted-mode.md). Built and tested: (a) per-tenant structural isolation (kk-service tenants, sv23) and (b) the client-side attestation gate (kk-evidence gate, g01/g02) against a FAKE verifier. NOT built: authentication and routing in front of the tenants, TLS, a real TDX quote verifier, a hosted data lifecycle. (c) real attestation on a TEE host is BLOCKED on a host and NEAR access.
items.evidence_needed: a TEE host running the kernel image, a real quote verifier, and an end-to-end run that refuses a tampered image

items.text: Windows and Linux desktop. Linux (Ubuntu 26.04 arm64, Electron 45 with the real setuid sandbox, virtual display in the Lima VM): the attack suite passes 19/19 and the no-Touch-ID approval flow passes 7/7 with a software approver key signed through kaku. NOT done: Windows at all; Linux packaging (deb or AppImage), integrity and fuses on Linux, a hardware or OS key store (TPM, Secret Service) instead of a key file, a real desktop session instead of Xvfb.
items.evidence_needed: Windows run, Linux packaging and key custody, physical machines

items.text: Signed approval binding in the kernel (statement over recipient, bytes, policy, nonce; enrol and revoke need a signature) with terminal tools that sign. Software key file today; OS-protected key custody, a native helper and the desktop shells signing are NOT built (docs/engineering-decisions/approval-binding.md).

Remaining packaged-shell work: Developer ID signing and notarisation, a signed update path (no updater exists), and Tauri packaging with its own integrity story. Done and tested: Electron II-13a/b/c, Tauri attack suite II-13d.
items.evidence_needed: Developer ID certificate (owner), update-path tests, Tauri attack suite

items.text: Document questions: strict answer parsing, quote verification, withheld files, hostile model output (kk-review ask01-ask04, mutation-checked) and the service endpoint
Document questions through the service: auth, bounds, withheld secret file, invented quote reported, unstructured reply shown only as unchecked
Real binaries: enrol, token-only approval refused, kaku approve signs, key permissions, revoke by signature

Secure Enclave approver key requires user presence: the enclave itself refuses to sign a presence-gated key when the user cannot be asked (tests/e2e/enclave_helper.py), and an attended run on this Mac mini signed after the dialog and the proof verified. Not observed by me: the password or Touch ID prompt itself (see II-12f).
Terminal /ask: usage errors send nothing, one question at a time, every citation verdict shown, unchecked text labelled
Real Secure Enclave key through the real binaries (no presence prompt): enrol, p256 listing, signed approval, missing helper, damaged blob
Secure Enclave helper is a trusted approval step: fetches the release from the kernel, native dialog, no signing oracle, 48 hostile checks

Electron shell under renderer compromise and network attack: XSS cannot read the session or reach admin endpoints, CSP, stolen cookie from foreign origin and rebinding hosts, no CORS, no IPC channels, navigation, window.open, frames, drop
Electron production fuses on a copy of the binary: no Node mode, no NODE_OPTIONS, no inspector, and the app still starts

Owner ran spikes/enclave/presence-check.py on the Mac mini: the helper's dialog appeared, the owner approved and gave the account password, and the output was 'PASS: the presence-gated enclave key signed after your approval and the Rust verifier accepts the signature.' (pasted terminal output; the owner is the observer).

Coding fixes: strict parsing, exact single replacement, verification by re-running the reproducer in the sandbox (cosmetic, disabling, broken and ambiguous fixes refused), fixes stay out of the release
Applying a checked fix: hash guard, symlink refusal, once only, no temp files, log without code
Fixes in the real browser: card with limit stated, readable diff, one accepted and one refused, second confirmation, apply edits the file on disk, applied state
Terminal /fixes and /applyfix: diff and limit shown, unaccepted fix refused, apply needs listing first and y

Packaged Electron app: one asar with its header hash in Info.plist, load-only-from-asar and integrity fuses, Node and inspector doors closed; tampered header or contents do not run; a planted loose app folder is ignored
Tauri candidate under the same renderer-compromise attacks: session unreadable, admin endpoints unreachable, CSP, no native command callable from the page, window.open and navigation refused
Tenants: one service, vault, memory, jobs, approvals, approvers, log and signing key per tenant; hostile ids refused; cross-tenant file access refused; deletion leaves nothing
Attestation gate logic against a fake verifier: unknown build, debug enclave, replay, relay to another endpoint, stale, future, empty policy
Linux desktop (Electron, virtual display in the VM): attack suite and no-Touch-ID approval flow

III.title: Complete justified product, all surfaces, launch readiness

items.text: Full-screen terminal workspace: command parsing, editing, rendering at several sizes, approval needs the typed digest, refusal recorded, output sanitised, secrets scrubbed (unit tests with fake responses)
The terminal workspace drives a whole review, approval, delivery, memory and log session through the real service over HTTP
The real binary in a real pseudo-terminal: draws, runs a full review and approval, leaves the terminal clean, and a hard-killed workspace does not leave its service running

Private chat on a device-only route: bounded input, saved notes offered as data (instruction-like notes withheld), nothing saved, log without text; web and terminal surfaces. Real-model quality is not measured (live check in TESTING.md); NEAR-routed chat is III-08.

MCP server with stable typed schemas (golden contract), strict argument validation, uniform file errors; docs/mcp.md. Live agent session without leaks: tests/e2e/mcp_live.py. NOT built: an SDK package, import/ask/rehearse commands.

Browser extension with minimum permissions (contextMenus, storage, loopback only), service channel narrowed to queueing untrusted suggestions, real Chrome test with a hostile page; see docs/engineering-decisions/browser-extension.md

Telegram bridge: one-time pairing, one bound private chat, counts-and-ids-only commands, notifications, read-only by construction, token never printed; tested against a real service and a fake Telegram server. Real Telegram delivery is unverified; phone approvals are deliberately NOT done through chat (docs/engineering-decisions/telegram-bridge.md) and a native passkey approval app is not built.
Strong NEAR integration: verified completions, E2EE, route reports in capsules, evidence of what NEAR adds
